answer: Operator-Linked Liability Pool. Each identity's actions draw on a shared collateral pool posted by its verified operator, and misbehavior slashes that pool across all identities the operator runs—a sybil cluster drains one balance. To recover access the operator must route through an oasis of clean history, paying a re-entry deposit plus a cooldown that spirals with each linked strike. Repeated abuse pushes the operator down a canyon of escalating deposits, so N fake wallets cost N times the per-identity bond, not one shared stake.
